title: Recognition of truncated simplicial objects by faces and degeneracies
statement:
Let $N\geq0$, let $\mathcal C$ be a category, and let $\Delta_{\leq N}$ be the category of finite ordinals $[r]=\{0<\cdots<r\}$, $0\leq r\leq N$, and order-preserving maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. Give objects $U_0,\ldots,U_N$, maps $d_i:U_r\to U_{r-1}$ for $1\leq r\leq N$, $0\leq i\leq r$, and maps $s_i:U_r\to U_{r+1}$ for $0\leq r<N$, $0\leq i\leq r$. Assume all the following identities whenever every degree occurring is between $0$ and $N$:
$$d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i\ (i<j),\qquad d_i s_j=s_{j-1}d_i\ (i<j),\qquad d_j s_j=1=d_{j+1}s_j,$$
$$d_i s_j=s_j d_{i-1}\ (i>j+1),\qquad s_i s_j=s_{j+1}s_i\ (i\leq j).$$
There is a unique functor $U:\Delta_{\leq N}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ with these objects and these maps as its coface and codegeneracy operators. Here $\delta_i:[r-1]\to[r]$ omits $i$, $\sigma_i:[r+1]\to[r]$ repeats $i$, and composition in the displayed formulas is read right to left. Every arrow of $\Delta_{\leq N}$ is a composite of these cofaces and codegeneracies with intermediate degrees at most $N$; every surjective arrow is a composite of codegeneracies with intermediate degrees at most $N$. For any two such functors, a family of component maps is a natural transformation if and only if it commutes with every displayed face and degeneracy operator.

source.place: Tags 0166 (lemma-face-degeneracy), 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), and 016B (lemma-characterize-simplicial-object), bounded-degree form for Definition 0180 (definition-truncated-simplicial-object): the normal form first decreases then increases the ordinal degree and stays within the maximum endpoint degree.

proof.text: Work in the full subcategory $\Delta_{\leq N}$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. Construct a word for $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ by induction on $a+b$. If a value $i$ is missing, necessarily $b>0$; define $\psi(x)=\alpha(x)$ below $i$ and $\psi(x)=\alpha(x)-1$ above $i$. Then $\alpha=\delta_i\psi$ and the induction applies to $[a]\to[b-1]$. Otherwise $\alpha$ is surjective. If it is not injective, monotonicity gives an adjacent equality $\alpha(j)=\alpha(j+1)$; delete the second entry to obtain $\psi:[a-1]\to[b]$ and $\alpha=\psi\sigma_j$, again decreasing $a+b$. A bijective monotone map between finite ordinals is the identity. All intermediate degrees stay below $\max(a,b)\leq N$. Starting with a surjection, the second reduction remains surjective, so it yields a word consisting only of codegeneracies.

Read any generator word in execution order from source to target, with all its vertex degrees in $[0,N]$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. At an adjacent coface followed by a codegeneracy, replace $\sigma_j\delta_i$ by $\delta_i\sigma_{j-1}$ if $i<j$, by the empty word if $i=j$ or $j+1$, and by $\delta_{i-1}\sigma_j$ if $i>j+1$. These are exactly the opposites of the assumed mixed identities. A noncancelling replacement lowers the peak degree by two, preserving its endpoints. When the endpoints have degree zero only the cancelling cases are possible, so no negative degree is introduced. Termination follows lexicographically from word length and the number of pairs in which a coface precedes a codegeneracy: cancellation decreases length, and exchange decreases the latter count by one. The result executes all codegeneracies first and all cofaces second, thus has composite $D\circ S$ with $S$ surjective and $D$ injective, entirely in the retained degrees.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), omitted mixed-word reduction, supplied here using the relations of Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy) (2)-(4).

proof.text: Take two retained-degree words with the same value $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$, and reduce each as in the preceding step to $D\circ S$ and $D^{\prime}\circ S^{\prime}$. Their middle ordinal is the ordered image of $\alpha$: surjectivity of $S$ makes the image of $D$ equal to that image, and an increasing injection is uniquely determined by its image. Thus both middle degrees are $|\operatorname{im}\alpha|-1$, $D=D^{\prime}$ as ordered-set maps, and injectivity of $D$ gives $S=S^{\prime}$. Apply [lem-sfb-pure-coface-word-relations] to the two coface blocks and [lem-sfb-pure-codegeneracy-word-relations] to the two codegeneracy blocks. Their transformations use only degrees between their respective endpoints, hence at most $N$. Combining them with the two mixed reductions gives a derivation between the original words using only the retained-degree relations.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), completeness via the ordered-image factorization and the pure-block relations.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$, choose the word of step 1 and evaluate it contravariantly, replacing $\delta_i$ by $d_i$, $\sigma_i$ by $s_i$, and the empty word by $1$. Every replacement in steps 2 and 3 preserves this value by precisely the identities assumed in the statement, including their contexts by associativity. Hence the value is independent of the chosen word. Concatenation of words gives $U(\beta\alpha)=U(\alpha)U(\beta)$; the empty word gives $U(1)=1$. These values define the required functor [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] and have the specified generator values. Any other such functor agrees on every word, so step 1 gives uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 016B (lemma-characterize-simplicial-object) (2), evaluation argument restricted to Definition 0180.

proof.text: For functors $U,V$ and a family $\eta_r:U_r\to V_r$, the equation $\eta_aU(\alpha)=V(\alpha)\eta_b$ for $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ is automatic for identities. If it holds for $\alpha$ and $\beta:[b]\to[c]$, then $\eta_aU(\alpha)U(\beta)=V(\alpha)\eta_bU(\beta)=V(\alpha)V(\beta)\eta_c$. Thus commuting with all generators implies this equation for every word, hence every arrow by step 1. Conversely naturality gives it on each generator. This is exactly the definition of a morphism of truncated simplicial objects [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. For $N=0$ the sole arrow is the identity, so the same argument covers the empty generator family.

F : SimplicialObject.Truncated C N, F.obj = U ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 2)), HEq (F.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ N i (by change n ≤ N; omega) hn).op) (d n hn i)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 1)), HEq (F.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ N i hn (by change n ≤ N; omega)).op) (s n hn i))) ∧ (∀ (a b : SimplexCategory.Truncated N) (f : a ⟶ b), MorphismProperty.multiplicativeClosure (fun _ _ g ↦ (∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 2)), Arrow.mk g = Arrow.mk (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ N i (by change n ≤ N; omega) hn)) ∨ (∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 1)), Arrow.mk g = Arrow.mk (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ N i hn (by change n ≤ N; omega)))) f) ∧ (∀ (a b : SimplexCategory.Truncated N) (f : a ⟶ b), Function.Surjective f.hom.toOrderHom → MorphismProperty.multiplicativeClosure (fun _ _ g ↦ ∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 1)), Arrow.mk g = Arrow.mk (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ N i hn (by change n ≤ N; omega))) f) ∧ (∀ (F G : SimplicialObject.Truncated C N) (η : ∀ a, F.obj a ⟶ G.obj a), (∀ (a b : (SimplexCategory.Truncated N)ᵒᵖ) (f : a ⟶ b), F.map f ≫ η b = η a ≫ G.map f) ↔ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 2)), F.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ N i (by change n ≤ N; omega) hn).op ≫ η (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk n, by change n ≤ N; omega⟩) = η (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1), hn⟩) ≫ G.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ N i (by change n ≤ N; omega) hn).op) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 ≤ N) (i : Fin (n + 1)), F.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ N i hn (by change n ≤ N; omega)).op ≫ η (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1), hn⟩) = η (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk n, by change n ≤ N; omega⟩) ≫ G.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ N i hn (by change n ≤ N; omega)).op))

reviewed_lean.note: I checked the statement field: it matches the file verbatim. The only stmt_dep is def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton (Mathlib SimplicialObject.Truncated). I read the Mathlib signatures of SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ/σ; their bound-argument orders are used correctly. I reindexed all six identity hypotheses by hand: hdd, hds_lt, hds_self, hds_succ, hds_gt and hss equal Mathlib's δ_comp_δ, δ_comp_σ_of_le, the two retraction identities, δ_comp_σ_of_gt and σ_comp_σ. Each covers the full index range, applies exactly when all degrees are in [0,N], and adds no stronger assumption. Conclusions: a single (not nested) ∃! functor with F.obj = U and HEq on the generators; generation by δ/σ in multiplicativeClosure inside Truncated N; surjections generated by σ alone; naturality iff commuting with the generators, endpoints oriented correctly. Edge cases N=0, N=1, boundary indices, empty C and independent universes are covered. No definitions, no hollow data, sorry-only proof. Docstrings carry the source place, the blueprint id and the five proof steps. The private import of the proof dep PureCofaceWordRelations is harmless. No compile, since no file was changed.
